source_read: PMC HTML, PMC8351054 (Acad Forensic Pathol 2019;9(1-2):66-80; title confirmed in own tab): all sections, Tables 1-4 (as text, garbled cells noted), author roles, footnotes (ethics, human rights, consent, disclosures, funding), article notes (received 10 Dec 2018, accepted 31 Jan 2019), reference list. Figure 1 is a region map; no values needed. Blind notes written before the card was opened. P-values recomputed from printed counts (scipy, chi-square uncorrected and Yates, Fisher). Paragraph counts are running-text only: Introduction 5; Methods > Study Population 1, Survey Design and Administration 3, Statistical Analysis 1; Results 9 (the (a)-(d) barriers are inline in the 9th paragraph, not a list); Discussion 7; Limitations 2; Conclusion 2.

key_findings.note: 'Four' regional offices comes from Results 1st paragraph and Table 1, not the Introduction. The Introduction (4th paragraph) cites reference 9 (Manini 2011, agreement between medical examiners and toxicologists) for state funding of toxicology, which looks like a miscitation.
Implied county counts per region (14/32, 22/51, 4/13, 8/24) sum to 120.
The text names years, training, jurisdiction, budget and region. Concurrent position (p=0.84) is only in Table 2.
Fisher p 0.0033 matches the printed value.
Fisher 0.0359 recomputed. Results 3rd paragraph calls the 38% 'data not shown', but it is in Table 4 (the duplicated toxicology row). The 25% for autopsy is not tabulated.
The text cites Table 3 for 76% and 29%, but Table 3 has only the finances item, and that item is 'at some point', not 'always'. Fisher 0.1052 recomputed.
Training 59% and medical examiner help 62% are text only; Table 3 holds information gained and kits.

reporting_issues.note: Add to the consequence: if the all-respondents column were right, the labels in Tables 2-4 would be swapped and every experience contrast would reverse. Three placements agree on 27/20: the phase columns, the Table 2-4 headings and the Table 2 row counts. The all-respondents column and the text are therefore the likelier error. The text's 58% is 27/47 = 57.4% double-rounded.
Fisher 0.1052 and 0.0861 recomputed. Results 3rd paragraph correctly calls the 0.0518 rows non-significant.
Recomputed: 7/22 vs 7/25 chi-square 0.775, Fisher 1.0; 8/39 vs 1/7 chi-square 0.702, Fisher 1.0.
Fisher 0.0617 and 0.0636. Fisher matches the printed values in other rows (0.0431, 0.0033, 0.0026), so the test was chosen row by row.

risk_of_bias.note: JBI prevalence; the editors' summary is high. Wilson intervals recomputed (31.7-48.9%, 44.3-71.2%, 48.4-74.8%). The count of 82 tests, 16 at p<0.05 and 4 more flagged was recounted from Tables 2-4.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. One addition: the card calls the abstract's 'uptake not yet complete' restrained. Its basis is a non sequitur, though: coroners already testing before the mandate would also report no increase, and no item asked whether all decedents are tested (Discussion 1st paragraph).

missed: Discussion 2nd paragraph says experience 'affected the uptake of toxicology testing requests', and the 6th says location 'impacted the uptake'. But Table 2's more-toxicology item does not differ by years (55.6% vs 60%, p=0.76) or region (59.1% vs 57.7%, p=0.92). The uptake claims rest on attitude and barrier items.

Discussion 4th paragraph says toxicology training 'addresses the barrier of restricted space' on the certificate. Results 9th paragraph reports the opposite pattern: trained coroners cited lack of room more often (88% vs 50%).
Discussion 5th paragraph says the epidemic 'more than quadrupled coroner caseloads' with no data or citation; the survey measured only whether caseloads had risen.
